title: XPeng's IRON humanoid robot first to autonomously walk off its own production line - TCR 09/08/26
description:
XPeng's IRON humanoid walked off the world's first automated humanoid production line in Guangzhou with XPeng saying more than 80% of its core processes are automated, Malaysia weighed Huawei Ascend chips for a RM2 billion sovereign AI build that Bloomberg reports could become the first known case of a national government choosing Chinese silicon over American, and OpenAI revised GPT-6 Astra's benchmark numbers after launch as the ARC Prize Foundation independently confirmed results that differed by about 36 points across two reported setups.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-8-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:46 XPeng's IRON walks off the automated line
3:31 Malaysia weighs Huawei silicon for sovereign AI
6:26 OpenAI revises Astra's benchmarks after launch
9:22 NHS opt-outs rise over Palantir mistrust
12:08 Aging clocks read a signal inside a real trial
15:01 Close

This episode covers XPeng's IRON humanoid line and its shared EV supply chain, Malaysia weighing Huawei's Ascend accelerators for sovereign AI, OpenAI's post-launch Astra benchmark revisions and the ARC Prize Foundation's independent audit, 60,000 NHS patients withdrawing records over Palantir mistrust, and six proteomic aging clocks reading younger inside a finished lung-disease trial.

XPeng's IRON walked off an automated line that XPeng says automates more than 80% of its core processes and XPeng says shares over 85% of its supply chain with the company's electric-car business, the machinery XPeng is betting could turn one impressive unit into thousands at a falling cost. In Malaysia, some forecasts expect a memory shortage to run through 2030, and a reported Huawei discount tipped a sovereign AI build toward Chinese silicon, the condition under which chip export controls leak first. OpenAI moved several Astra figures after launch, and the ARC Prize Foundation confirmed Astra's roughly 99.9% result with OpenAI's custom harness and 62.7% result with ARC Prize's standard harness from outside the lab, so the gap sits documented by the party that gains nothing from hiding it. In England, NHS figures recorded roughly 60,000 additional national data opt-outs amid Palantir mistrust, and a minister conceded the NHS owns its data models and could migrate them. Six aging clocks built by different teams on different training data all read treated patients younger inside a finished lung-drug trial, opening a shortcut around the decades-long longevity study.
